source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-15
statement: Classic conformance A-15 (T1): Ctrl+Enter — Commit and stay. With several cells selected, the entry goes into every one of them; relative references adjust cell by cell.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-16
statement: Classic conformance A-16 (T1): Ctrl+Shift+Enter — Commit as a legacy array formula over the selection, shown in braces. Part of it cannot be changed alone; Excel's message says so.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-17
statement: Classic conformance A-17 (T1): Esc — Cancels the entry. The cell is exactly as it was.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-18
statement: Classic conformance A-18 (T1): Click another cell, while entering — For a value: commit, and select the clicked cell. For a formula, where a reference may go: insert the reference (Part 4).
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-19
statement: Classic conformance A-19 (T1): Enter or Tab inside a selection — Commit and move to the next cell within the selection, wrapping at its end. Shift reverses. Ctrl+. moves the active cell to the next corner.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-20
statement: Classic conformance A-20 (T1): How an entry is read — As Excel reads it in the current locale. `5%` is 0.05 with a percent format. `1/2` is a date; `0 1/2` is a half. `1e3`, `$1,000` and `(100)` are numbers. A leading apostrophe forces text. `=`, `+`, `-` and `@` start a formula. Dates and times take the matching format. Digits beyond the fifteenth are lost exactly as in Excel.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-21
statement: Classic conformance A-21 (T1): An entry Excel would refuse — Refused with Excel's message, and with Excel's proposed correction where it offers one. The cell stays in Edit.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-22
statement: Classic conformance A-22 (T2): Text AutoComplete — In a column, the start of an existing entry proposes the rest. Enter accepts; continuing to type declines. Alt+↓ opens the list of the column's entries.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T2).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-23
statement: Classic conformance A-23 (T1): Data validation — An entry that breaks a rule is handled by the rule's style. Stop refuses. Warning and Information ask. The rule's own title and message are used.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-24
statement: Classic conformance A-24 (T1): Tables — Typing in the row under a table, or the column beside it, extends the table. A formula typed in a table column fills the column. Ctrl+Z once takes back the automatic part, twice the entry.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-25
statement: Classic conformance A-25 (T1): Dynamic arrays — A formula that returns an array spills. A blocked spill gives `#SPILL!`. Cells of a spill other than its first show the formula greyed and cannot be edited. `@` appears where Excel shows it.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-26
statement: Classic conformance A-26 (T1): A loop, with iteration off — Excel's result: zero, and the circular state reported, with the cell named.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 2. Committing, cancelling and what an entry means) A-27
statement: Classic conformance A-27 (T1): Protected sheets — Typing in a locked cell is refused with Excel's message. Tab moves among unlocked cells only.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-28
statement: Classic conformance A-28 (T1): F4, while editing — Cycles the reference at the caret: `A1`, `$A$1`, `A$1`, `$A1`, `A1`. Both ends of a range cycle together. With text selected, every reference in the selection cycles.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-29
statement: Classic conformance A-29 (T1): F4, in Ready — Repeats the last command, as Ctrl+Y does when there is nothing to redo.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-30
statement: Classic conformance A-30 (T1): F9, while editing — Replaces the selected part of the formula, or all of it, with its value, inside the edit. Esc restores the formula. Enter would keep the value.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-31
statement: Classic conformance A-31 (T1): F9, Shift+F9, Ctrl+Alt+F9, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F9, in Ready — Calculate all open workbooks. Calculate the active sheet. Calculate everything whether changed or not. Rebuild dependencies, then calculate everything.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-32
statement: Classic conformance A-32 (T1): F3, Ctrl+F3, Ctrl+Shift+F3 — Paste Name, while editing. Name Manager. Create names from the selection's labels.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-33
statement: Classic conformance A-33 (T1): Shift+F3 — Insert Function. Here it opens the Formula Explorer at Functions, with Excel's search, categories and argument fields. Ctrl+A after a function's name opens its arguments. Ctrl+Shift+A inserts the argument names.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-34
statement: Classic conformance A-34 (T1): Formula AutoComplete — After `=` and a letter, a list of functions, names and tables. ↑ and ↓ move. Tab inserts. Esc closes the list and keeps the entry. Inside a table reference, `[` lists columns, `@` means this row, `#` lists the special items.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-35
statement: Classic conformance A-35 (T1): The function tip — Shows the signature with the current argument in bold. A click on an argument selects it in the formula. A click on the function's name opens its help.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-36
statement: Classic conformance A-36 (T1): The range finder — While a formula is edited, each referenced range is outlined on the grid. Dragging an outline moves the reference. Dragging its corner resizes it. The text follows.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-37
statement: Classic conformance A-37 (T1): Ctrl+\` — Shows formulas in cells in place of values, and widens the columns, as Excel does. Again restores.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-38

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-39

why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-40
statement: Classic conformance A-40 (T2): Ctrl+' and Ctrl+Shift+" — Copy the formula, or the value, of the cell above into this one, and stay in Edit.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-41

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-42

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-43
statement: Classic conformance A-43 (T2): Alt, M, P; Alt, M, D; Alt, M, A, A — Draw tracer arrows to precedents, or to dependents; remove them. A dashed arrow to a sheet symbol means another sheet. A double-click on an arrow follows it.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T2).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-44

why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 3. Formula keys: F2, F3, F4, F9 and the rest) A-45

Alt+Shift+F10 opens the flag's menu, with Excel's choices, Ignore among them.
why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T2).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 4. Picking ranges while typing a formula) A-47

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 4. Picking ranges while typing a formula) A-48

why: Required for Excel for Windows parity (T1).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 4. Picking ranges while typing a formula) A-49

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 4. Picking ranges while typing a formula) A-50

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix A (Part 4. Picking ranges while typing a formula) A-52

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-1): Undo belongs to one workbook, names its steps, and survives macro runs and saves.
why: Excel's undo is shared by every open workbook and is emptied by a macro.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-2): The copy outline stands still. The Strip says what is on the clipboard.
why: Strand allows three animations; this is not one. Nothing is lost.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-3): References in a formula are numbered and drawn in the teal family; the one at the caret is amber.
why: Works without colour vision; red stays free for errors.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-4): No dialogs on opening for links, macros, loops or old formats. One notice line, the Overview and the Strip.
why: The user is in the file at once, and the facts stay on screen.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-5): An error has a red tick on the cell's left edge. A note has a teal fold.
why: Red means one thing. The cell's own formatting is untouched.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-6): Validation refusals, blocked spills and loops are explained at the cell, with the choices Excel's dialogs offer.
why: Nothing to dismiss; the context stays in view.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-7): The seam warns before commit when an entry overwrites a formula inside a run, pastes into hidden rows, or writes to grouped sheets.
why: The three commonest silent accidents are shown before they happen.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-8): Grouped sheets show "Group: 3 sheets" in amber in the Strip and on each grouped tab.
why: Excel says it only in the title bar.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-9): Below 40% zoom, block labels replace cell text.
why: Excel shows range names at 39% and below; this goes one step further and keeps text legible.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-10): A form control shows a ghost value while dragged. It still commits on release.
why: Feedback during the drag without extra recalculations.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-11): Shift+F3, Alt, M, V and Alt, M, P open DNA Calc's fuller tools at the matching facet.
why: The habit is kept and leads somewhere better.

statement: Deliberate difference from Excel (D-12): Not provided: the Office Clipboard pane, Research and Thesaurus, ink. Their keys answer "Not in DNA Calc" in the Strip.
why: No dead keys.

statement: Browser platform difference (N-1): An ordinary tab cannot receive Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab, F11 and, in some browsers, Ctrl+PageDown and Ctrl+PageUp. Handling: The installed window receives them all. In a tab, Ctrl+Alt+PageDown and PageUp change sheet and the palette covers the rest. The Strip says so once, naming the key. No key differs silently.
why: Ensures no shortcut or platform capability differs silently in the browser.

statement: Browser platform difference (N-2): Reading the clipboard may need the user's permission, and some formats may be withheld. Handling: Asked on the first paste. If a format was not available, the Strip says which and what was pasted instead.
why: Ensures no shortcut or platform capability differs silently in the browser.

statement: Browser platform difference (N-3): Some browsers take Alt for their own menu. Handling: Key tips can also be raised from the palette. The installed window has no such limit.
why: Ensures no shortcut or platform capability differs silently in the browser.

statement: Browser platform difference (N-4): The right mouse button. Handling: DNA Calc's menu on the stage; Shift+right-click gives the browser's.
why: Ensures no shortcut or platform capability differs silently in the browser.

statement: Browser platform difference (N-5): The Back button. Handling: It is the place history, the same as Alt+←.
why: Ensures no shortcut or platform capability differs silently in the browser.

statement: Browser platform difference (N-6): Native add-ins, macros that reach the machine, and links to local files. Handling: Not available. Saved values are shown with the `◊` and a reason, and "Open in the desktop app" is offered.
why: Ensures no shortcut or platform capability differs silently in the browser.

statement: All front-end requirements (R-1..R-106) are written to be directly testable, using 'model hash' (exact comparison of everything Excel reads from the file) to prove presentation-only and Esc-revert invariants.
why: Provides an objective oracle for non-mutation guarantees.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-1
statement: R-1: Every view is drawn inside the same shell, with Mast, Deck, Bridge, stage, panels and Strip in the same places. *Test:* the chrome regions occupy the same rectangles in all five views. [M0.1]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-2
statement: R-2: The Strip is visible in every view and under every skin, and always shows the mode word, calculation state, error count, outside-data state, macro state and agent state.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-3
statement: R-3: The address field shows the model address of the selection in every view. An address typed there, in Go To or in the palette selects that thing in the current view.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-4
statement: R-4: The formula bar shows the formula of the selected item in every view where the item stands for cells, and edits it with the keys of Appendix A, Part 3.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-5
statement: R-5: SELECTED and EDITING differ in three places at once: the item, the bar and the mode word. No other state changes all three.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-6
statement: R-6: After Esc the model hash equals the hash before the edit began. [A-17]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-7
statement: R-7: Esc steps back exactly one level, in this order: edit, preview, copy outline, popover, look-inside.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-8
statement: R-8: Every shortcut that is DNA Calc's own is Alt+Shift+key or Alt+Q. None takes a key listed in Appendix A.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-9
statement: R-9: The palette opens within 50 ms of Alt+Q. It finds commands, addresses, names, sheets, blocks and views, shows each command's key and key-tip path, and offers "Ask the agent" as its last row. [S7.1]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-10
statement: R-10: Alt shows key tips. On the first five uses in an installation it also shows the one-line summary of the Alt+Shift layer. [M1.3]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-11
statement: R-11: The peek card has the same content for the same object in every view. It appears after 500 ms of rest, never covers its object, and its content is also in the Details panel (Alt+Shift+D).

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-12
statement: R-12: Keyboard focus is always visible: an amber ring at least 2 px wide with a 1 px offset. When focus leaves the stage, the stage's selection is drawn hollow.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-13
statement: R-13: In DNA Calc's own marks, amber is used only for selection, focus and "now"; red only for errors; signal orange only for outside or volatile data; green only for fresh values. Each has a shape as well. *Test:* an audit of every use of the five tokens.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-14
statement: R-14: In every view a solid line means stated in the file, a dashed line inferred, a dotted line a ghost.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (The shell and what every view shares) R-15
statement: R-15: Nothing animates except the settle of selection and focus, the recalculation ripple (400 ms at most) and the halo on a view switch. All three stop under the reduced-motion setting.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Views and switching) R-16
statement: R-16: Alt+Shift+1 to 5 switch view. After the switch the selection stands for the same model objects. There and back restores the exact selection and scroll position. *Test:* a property test over random selections on the cast workbooks.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Views and switching) R-17
statement: R-17: After a switch the selected item is visible and outlined within 150 ms. Where the item is coarser than the selection, the Strip states the mapping. [S2.1]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Views and switching) R-18
statement: R-18: Alt+Shift+0 opens and closes the grid alongside. The selection is shared both ways. There are never more than two panes. [M4.3]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Views and switching) R-19
statement: R-19: A file's preferred view is applied when the file is first opened. A sheet's preferred view is shown as a badge on its tab and is never applied by a click on the tab.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Views and switching) R-20
statement: R-20: From every view, App included, the cells behind the selected item are one key away.
R-21: Every T1 item of Appendix A passes its scripted test on the cast workbooks. The differences from Excel are exactly those of Part 12.
R-22: Cell formatting is drawn as Excel draws it. No overlay is on by default in Classic.
R-23: The key-tip paths of A-139 to A-141 run the same commands whatever the Deck's layout or the skin.
R-24: While a formula is edited, each reference has a number and a tone shared by the text and by its outline on the grid. The reference at the caret is amber. [M8.1]
R-25: An entry that would overwrite a formula inside a run, paste into hidden rows or write to grouped sheets shows a warning in the seam before commit. [S3.7]
R-26: On opening, values from the file are shown within budget under an "as saved" mark that names the date of saving, until they are recalculated. [M1.2]
R-27: Under manual calculation, cells whose inputs have changed are hatched until calculated.
R-28: In a recalculation longer than 300 ms the Strip shows progress, pending cells are hatched, typing stays within its budget, and Esc interrupts. [S1.8]
R-29: After the first recalculation of an opened file, the number of values that differ from those saved is shown and leads to the list.
R-30: Opening a file never raises a dialog about links, macros, loops or file format.
R-31: Missing links, the macro state, manual calculation and hidden sheets are summed up in one notice line and in the Overview.
R-32: Errors are grouped by root. Each root states how many cells depend on it. Enter goes to the root. [S1.4]
R-33: Hidden and very hidden sheets are listed and can be looked at without changing the file.
R-34: The Mast's state word is one of: new, unchanged, saved, edited, "saved, layout edited", read-only. Undoing back to the opening state shows "unchanged". [S1.7]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Edits outside the grid) R-35
statement: R-35: Before commit, every gesture that changes the model, in any view, shows the cells, names and settings it will write, in Excel's syntax. Commit writes exactly that. *Test:* the seam's list equals the change journal.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Edits outside the grid) R-36
statement: R-36: Every model change made in any view can be reproduced by a person in Excel. A gesture that cannot is refused with a reason and an alternative. *Test:* the saved file opens in Excel without repair and shows identical values.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Edits outside the grid) R-37
statement: R-37: A presentation change alters no value, formula, name, format or setting. *Test:* the model hash is unchanged across 1,000 random presentation operations in each view.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Edits outside the grid) R-38
statement: R-38: Editing a run item writes relatively identical formulas to the whole run, as one undo step. [S2.5]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Edits outside the grid) R-39
statement: R-39: A run with an exception is shown as "n alike, m differ" in every view and print, with the exception one step away. [M2.2]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Edits outside the grid) R-40
statement: R-40: New model content is placed by the placement rule. The place is in the seam and can be changed before commit. [M4.1]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Edits outside the grid) R-41
statement: R-41: A view sort or view filter never changes Excel's filter state or row order, and is labelled as a view filter with its counts. [M3.2]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Edits outside the grid) R-42
statement: R-42: Prose can quote cells. A formula typed in prose is refused, with an offer to add it to the workbook. [S2.3]
R-43: A first visit offers a draft built from the readings, within 400 ms on the four small cast workbooks. Drafting leaves the model hash unchanged.
R-44: A frame shows its window of rows and "n of N". Folded columns and sections are named, with their exceptions and errors.
R-45: A value quoted in prose updates on recalculation and takes its cell's number format.
R-46: Reading density hides formulas and sets prose at about 68 characters. Changing density changes no content.
R-47: At 200% zoom prose reflows with no sideways scrolling; frames scroll inside themselves.

R-48: Every wire stands for at least one reference in a formula, and every reference between drawn items is covered by a wire or a bundle. The "x of y accounted for" line is exact. *Test:* compared against the dependency data on the cast workbooks.
R-49: Frames of inferred groups and blocks are dashed. Sheets, names and tables are solid.
R-50: A delay mark is drawn on a wire only where the system reports that read as last-pass. Otherwise the loop is drawn without one. [S4.4]
R-51: Typing `name = formula` on empty paper creates a labelled, named cell as the seam describes. Names not yet defined can be created as empty boxes. [S4.2, S4.3]
R-52: Closing a loop while iteration is off raises the three-way choice at the box, with no dialog. [M4.2]
R-53: The map is navigable by arrow keys, Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+], Enter, Esc and Tab, and every box has a text equivalent listing what it reads and what reads it.
R-54: While a formula is being edited, a click on a box inserts its address.
R-55: A drafted App page takes its inputs only from certain evidence: unlocked cells, validated cells and cells linked to controls. Others are added by the user or the agent.
R-56: Tab visits inputs only. A validation refusal appears in place with the workbook's own message, and Esc restores the previous value. [M5.1]
R-57: The scenarios listed are the workbook's Excel scenarios. "Save as scenario" writes one. Compare shows the difference for each output. [M5.2]
R-58: An output in error shows the error text, the red tick, a plain cause taken from the trace root, and an offer to undo. It never shows a blank or an earlier value. [S5.5]
R-59: Reset restores every input to its value at opening, as one undo step.
R-60: On closing with changes, the prompt lists the changes in plain words. [S5.8]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Inspector and Trace) R-61
statement: R-61: Trace opens on the active cell within 200 ms on the cast workbooks. It shows each argument with its value. For functions that test rows it shows the ladder, with the count that fails only each test. [M3.1]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Inspector and Trace) R-62
statement: R-62: Enter on a line of the ladder shows those rows as a view filter, with the count.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Inspector and Trace) R-63
statement: R-63: A hint carries its grade and never changes data.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Inspector and Trace) R-64
statement: R-64: The Calc instrument lists the last recalculation in evaluation order with values before and after. Recording writes nothing to the model. [M8.2]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Inspector and Trace) R-65
statement: R-65: Every instrument docks as a panel in every view, and enlarges to the Inspector view with its state kept. [S3.6]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Inspector and Trace) R-66
statement: R-66: With exactly two numeric cells selected, the Strip shows their difference.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Inspector and Trace) R-67
statement: R-67: Wherever a PivotTable appears, its last refresh and whether its source has changed since are shown.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Formula Explorer and lens) R-68
statement: R-68: Opened on a cell, the Explorer lists every precedent with its shown and stored value. Overriding one in the try column never changes the workbook. "Apply to cell" is the only action that writes. [M8.6]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Formula Explorer and lens) R-69
statement: R-69: Steps shows the value of every sub-expression and marks the first one that produced an error.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Formula Explorer and lens) R-70
statement: R-70: The number-format facet previews any format code on the cell's value and on positive, negative, zero and text samples, exactly as Excel would display them.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Formula Explorer and lens) R-71
statement: R-71: The conditional-format facet lists the rules that apply to the cell, in order, with which fired and why.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Formula Explorer and lens) R-72
statement: R-72: The standalone Explorer starts within 0.5 s, needs no workbook, loads an add-in behind the trust card, survives an add-in's failure, reloads a changed add-in without restarting, and saves as `.xlsx`. [S6]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Formula Explorer and lens) R-73
statement: R-73: The lens changes display only. Resting on a chip shows the plain reference. Inferred labels are visibly unlike defined names. With the lens on, the seam shows the Excel text that will be stored.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Formula Explorer and lens) R-74
statement: R-74: A formula that uses an add-in function is marked `◊`. Saving notes what Excel will show without the add-in. [S6.9]
R-75: Every reading shows its kind, label, grade and evidence. Each correction takes one gesture, is kept in the file, and is there on reopening. [M9.1]
R-76: No correction changes the model, except "Pin with a name", which says that it does.
R-77: When a file has been edited outside DNA Calc, view items are matched again on opening. Items that moved are marked "re-located". Items that cannot be matched are kept as orphans with a notice.
R-78: Every budget of section 6 holds on Inherited, and is measured on every build.
R-79: Every simplification states a count. *Test:* what is shown plus what is stated as not shown equals what exists.
R-80: Every declining state gives the size, the reason and at least two ways forward.
R-81: The default permission is Propose: nothing is written until accepted.
R-82: Each part of a proposal shows its cells, before and after, its effect on results as a count with examples, and the three checks. "No value changes" is computed, never asserted. [M7.1]
R-83: Acceptance is by part. Each accepted part is one named undo step. An undone part returns to pending. [S7.5]
R-84: Revert writes a new step. Where later edits conflict it refuses and explains. [S7.7]
R-85: A cell's history shows who changed it, when, through which proposal, and its content before and after. [M7.2]
R-86: The agent's marks are teal, dotted and badged, and never amber.
R-87: Changing settings, allowing macros, loading add-ins, saving, and sending data outside each require a question to the user.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Undo and clipboard) R-88
statement: R-88: Undo belongs to one workbook. Steps are named. A macro run, a fill, a paste and a run edit are each one step. Undo survives saving.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Undo and clipboard) R-89
statement: R-89: In any view, Ctrl+Z undoes the more recent of the last model step and that view's last presentation step. The Strip names what was undone and of which kind. [S4.9]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Undo and clipboard) R-90
statement: R-90: Copy places tab-separated text, HTML and a picture on the clipboard. Paste follows the table below. A paste that creates model content shows the seam first.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B R-90 clipboard table (Cells)
statement: Clipboard paste matrix for 'Cells': into Classic -> Excel's rules in full; into Notebook -> a frame that quotes them, or text; into Map -> boxes: cells and names, listed in the seam; into another program -> tab-separated text, an HTML table, a picture.
why: Defines exact cross-view and external clipboard semantics under R-90.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B R-90 clipboard table (A frame or formula item)
statement: Clipboard paste matrix for 'A frame or formula item': into Classic -> the cells behind it; into Notebook -> a second showing of the item; into Map -> the same; into another program -> a table of values; the formula as text.
why: Defines exact cross-view and external clipboard semantics under R-90.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B R-90 clipboard table (A box or frame of the map)
statement: Clipboard paste matrix for 'A box or frame of the map': into Classic -> its cells and names; into Notebook -> a quote of its value; into Map -> boxes, with name clashes listed; into another program -> a picture and `name = formula` lines.
why: Defines exact cross-view and external clipboard semantics under R-90.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B R-90 clipboard table (Trace or Issues rows)
statement: Clipboard paste matrix for 'Trace or Issues rows': into Classic -> addresses and values; into Notebook -> text with live quotes; into Map -> not offered; into another program -> an outline and a table.
why: Defines exact cross-view and external clipboard semantics under R-90.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B R-90 clipboard table (Text or a table from outside)
statement: Clipboard paste matrix for 'Text or a table from outside': into Classic -> Excel's rules; into Notebook -> a text item; a table asks "text or cells?"; into Map -> `name = formula` lines become boxes.
why: Defines exact cross-view and external clipboard semantics under R-90.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: R-91: A skin is a declaration. Applying any skin leaves the model hash unchanged.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: R-92: A new or changed skin is applied as a try-on with Keep, Edit and Discard; Esc discards. A declaration that breaks a rule is rejected with the reasons in plain words.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: R-93: No skin can hide the Strip's fixed readouts, re-bind a signal role, break a contrast pair, or remove Alt+Shift+1 and Alt+Shift+0.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: R-94: A skin that changes a key of Appendix A is labelled with the number of keys it changes.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Printing and macros) R-95
statement: R-95: Classic's printed pages match Excel's for the cast workbooks: the same count and the same breaks.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Printing and macros) R-96
statement: R-96: Every print from another view carries the file, the scenario in use and the time of the values.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Printing and macros) R-97
statement: R-97: Macros are off until allowed. A control that is blocked explains which procedure it would run and what that code calls. [S1.6]

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Printing and macros) R-98
statement: R-98: A macro run is one undo step. "Macro running · Esc interrupts" is visible for as long as it runs.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix B (Printing and macros) R-99
statement: R-99: The three view verbs work through `Application.Run`, and the same code fails harmlessly in Excel.
R-100: Every function can be reached and operated by keyboard alone. Every storyboard passes without a mouse.

R-101: To a screen reader the grid gives each cell's address, value, formula and state. The other views present their items as documents, trees or lists, with what each reads and what reads it. Changes in calculation state and error count are announced without interrupting.
R-102: Contrast meets Strand's law in all three themes: 4.5:1 for text and small marks, 3:1 for large text and meaningful shapes.
R-103: The stage zooms from 10% to 400%. Interface scale is separate. At 200% on a 1280 × 720 screen no function is lost, and the views other than Classic reflow.
R-104: No information is carried by colour alone or by motion alone.
R-105: A saved file opens in Excel without a repair prompt. View settings are in a part that Excel preserves. Saving notes anything Excel will show differently.
R-106: If the view part is lost, the model is intact and every view still works from the program's readings.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: System needs (C-1..C-50) state what the front end requires from the underlying engine/host in plain front-end terms without prescribing internal implementation, inheriting section 6 speed budgets.
why: Separates front-end contract requirements from backend architecture.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Opening and state) C-1
statement: C-1: Open a file in stages: first the sheet names and sizes, then the active sheet's saved values and formats, then the rest, reporting progress throughout.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Opening and state) C-2
statement: C-2: Be given the values saved in the file separately from recalculated values, with the date and the program that saved them.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Opening and state) C-3
statement: C-3: Know, for any cell, whether its value has been calculated since loading and since its inputs last changed.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Opening and state) C-4
statement: C-4: Be told which cells changed after a recalculation, with old and new values, and what set the recalculation off: an edit, F9, a live source or a macro.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Opening and state) C-5
statement: C-5: Be told the order in which cells were evaluated in the last recalculation.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Opening and state) C-6
statement: C-6: Know how far a running calculation has got, be able to interrupt it, and be able to read values and accept typing meanwhile.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Opening and state) C-7
statement: C-7: Know the workbook's calculation settings (mode, iteration, maximum iterations, maximum change, precision as displayed, the date system) and change them as a user could.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-8
statement: C-8: Know which cells a formula depends on, and which depend on it, directly and in full, and have this summarised by block and by sheet with counts.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-9
statement: C-9: Know the dependencies that pass through names, tables, spills and functions that build references, and have the dynamic ones marked as such.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-10
statement: C-10: Know references from name to name and from name to cell as names, not flattened to cells.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-11
statement: C-11: Know which formulas on a sheet are identical in relative terms, that is, the runs, and be told when a run gains or loses a member.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-12
statement: C-12: Get the structure of a formula, with each part's position in the text.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-13
statement: C-13: Turn a structure back into exact Excel text; replace one reference with another; rename a name everywhere it is used.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-14
statement: C-14: Evaluate a formula step by step: the value of every sub-expression, and which one first produced an error.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-15
statement: C-15: For functions that test rows (SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS, FILTER and the lookups): which rows passed each test, which fail only one test, and which values were skipped and why.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-16
statement: C-16: For any error value, the cell or cells where it first arose.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-17
statement: C-17: Evaluate a formula, or a set of pending edits, without committing them, and report which values would change.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-18
statement: C-18: Know before commit whether a pending edit would close a loop, block a spill or break a validation rule.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-19
statement: C-19: Know each loop: the cells that form it.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-20
statement: C-20: Know for a spill its first cell, its extent and what blocks it.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-21
statement: C-21: Inside a loop under iteration, know for each reference whether its reader saw this pass's value or the previous pass's.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Dependencies and structure) C-22
statement: C-22: Know how an iteration ended: the passes run, and whether the change limit was met.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-23
statement: C-23: Tables: name, range, columns with their types, totals row, filter and sort state; and be told when a table grows.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-24
statement: C-24: PivotTables: source, fields, time of last refresh, and whether the source has changed since.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-25
statement: C-25: Data tables with their input cells. Scenarios with their changing cells and values; apply one, create one, and produce a scenario summary without adding a sheet.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-26
statement: C-26: Form controls with their linked cells, limits and steps; write through one as a user's click would.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-27
statement: C-27: Validation rules and their messages for a cell; test a candidate value against them.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-28
statement: C-28: Conditional formats: the rules that apply to a cell, their order, and which fired.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-29
statement: C-29: Number formats: show any value under any format code exactly as Excel would, colours and locale included, and tell the stored value from the shown one.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-30
statement: C-30: Protection: locked and hidden flags, sheet and workbook protection, and what each permits.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-31
statement: C-31: Sheet visibility, very hidden included; read a hidden sheet without changing its state.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-32
statement: C-32: Charts, shapes and pictures: their names and source ranges, and a rendering of each.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-33
statement: C-33: Print set-up, and pagination exactly as Excel would paginate.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (What workbooks hold) C-34
statement: C-34: Comments and notes: read, add, edit, remove.
C-35: External links: the target, found or missing, the values saved in the file, the last update. RTD topics: server, topic, last value and its time, and each update as an event.
C-36: Which functions in use are volatile, and which come from add-ins.

C-37: Add-ins: load, unload and reload one; what it registered (names, arguments, help text, flags); call one of its functions with given arguments; time the call; and be told when the add-in fails, without the application failing.

C-38: Macros: list modules and procedures without running anything; what each control and event calls; which object-model calls a procedure contains; run one with the ability to interrupt; and be told what the run changed.
C-39: Receive a macro's requests to switch view, select, show a panel, set status text or show a dialog.

source: pro19-fable/answer.md Appendix C (Changes and history) C-40

statement: C-50: Answer all of the above on a workbook the size of Inherited within the budgets of section 6, or say that an answer is partial and how partial.
Classic never alters how it draws cells because of a pattern reading; readings surface in Classic solely via Details, Outline, and optional block outlines below 40% zoom.
why: Protects Classic's visual fidelity while still exposing structural insights.

statement: Pattern D-1 (Sheet as database): *A person sees* one header row, one kind of thing per row, no gaps, and usually a filter. *The program sees* a table object (certain), or a filled rectangle with one header row and one data type per column that criteria functions or a pivot read (likely). *Correct by* moving the header row, extending the range, or "Make it a table" (Excel's Ctrl+T, a model edit). *Classic:* row count in Details. *Inspector:* column types, blanks, numbers stored as text, duplicate keys. *Notebook:* a frame; never one item per formula. *Map:* one box, with the columns that are read listed on it. *App:* a frame with search and a view filter; never an input.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-2 (Inputs and assumptions): *A person sees* labelled constants set apart, often coloured, often on a sheet named for them. *The program sees* constants with a label beside or above that formulas read: certain where the cell is unlocked on a protected sheet, validated or linked to a control; likely otherwise. *Correct by* "Not an input" or "Also an input" on any cell, and by editing its label. *Classic:* the provenance overlay shows them in the constant ink. *Inspector:* each input with the number of results it reaches. *Notebook:* the opening section, each input as a value item. *Map:* boxes in the constant ink at the left. *App:* the fields.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-3 (Calculation block): *A person sees* a rectangle of formulas with labels down one side and a heading above. *The program sees* adjacent runs sharing an axis, bounded by blank rows or columns (likely). *Correct by* extend, shrink, split, merge, rename. *Inspector:* its inputs, its outputs and its exceptions. *Notebook:* a section, each row a formula item, with one frame of values. *Map:* a dashed frame, its rows as boxes one zoom level in. *App:* nothing, unless a row is chosen as an output.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-4 (Time series, periods across): *A person sees* months or years along the top and the same formula across. *The program sees* a header of dates or period labels in equal steps (certain when they are true dates) over rows that are each one run (likely). *Correct by* naming the header row, setting the period, marking where history ends and forecast begins. *Inspector:* runs with their exceptions; the first period where a row's formula changes. *Notebook:* a frame with periods across and the lens form `Customers[prev]`. *Map:* `[t-1]` on rows that read their own previous period. *App:* a chart over the periods.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.
evidence: D-4; Budget `Monthly`; Loan's schedule runs down

statement: Pattern D-5 (Scenarios): *A person sees* columns headed Base and Downside with a cell that picks one, or knows the Scenario Manager was used. *The program sees* saved scenarios (certain), or parallel input columns read through CHOOSE, INDEX or IF on one cell (likely). *Correct by* naming the selector and the columns. *Inspector:* the inputs that differ between scenarios, and the results that move. *Notebook:* a scenario control at the top; quoted values follow it. *Map:* a switch box feeding the "in use" column. *App:* chips, Compare, Save as scenario.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.
evidence: D-5; Budget's two columns and selector; Loan's saved scenarios

statement: Pattern D-6 (Sensitivity table): *A person sees* a grid of results with input values along two edges and a formula in the corner. *The program sees* a data table (certain). *Correct by* nothing: it is stated in the file. *Inspector:* its row and column input cells; the cost, "recalculates the model 25 times". *Notebook:* a frame with both axes named. *Map:* a box marked "runs this part N times". *App:* a shaded table, read only.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.
evidence: D-6; none in the cast; common beside a Loan

statement: Pattern D-7 (Reference table): *A person sees* a small list of codes and meanings, off to one side. *The program sees* a block of constants read by lookup functions or by a validation list (likely). *Correct by* naming the key column. *Inspector:* keys looked up and not found; duplicate keys. *Notebook:* a frame marked lookup, after the section that uses it. *Map:* a side box with join wires labelled by key. *App:* the source of a drop-down.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-8 (Pipeline across sheets): *A person sees* sheets ordered left to right from raw to finished. *The program sees* references between sheets that run one way (likely; certain that no reference runs back). *Correct by* reordering the stages or leaving a sheet out. *Inspector:* any reference that runs against the flow. *Notebook:* the Across layout. *Map:* the sheet zoom, laid left to right. *App:* inputs from the first stage, outputs from the last.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.
evidence: D-8; Budget: Inputs, Monthly, Summary; Inherited: Deals, Positions, P&L by Desk, Summary

statement: Pattern D-9 (Running balance): *A person sees* opening, movement, closing, repeated down or across. *The program sees* a run in which each cell reads its neighbour in the run (likely). *Correct by* marking the opening cell. *Inspector:* where the chain is broken or overwritten. *Notebook:* one item, `Balance = Balance[prev] − Principal`, with its opening value stated. *Map:* a box with `[t-1]`. *App:* a line chart.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-10 (Deliberate circular reference): *A person* knows it because they built it, or because Excel complained. *The program sees* a loop that exists while iteration is on (certain); with iteration off, a loop is reported as an error state, as in Excel. *Correct by* marking a loop "intended" or "accidental", which changes only how loudly it is reported. *Classic:* the Strip's state. *Inspector:* the loop's cells, the settings, how the last iteration ended. *Notebook:* a note on the item, "reads its own last value". *Map:* the loop, with delay marks where they can be reported. *App:* an F9 step control.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-11 (Simulation): *A person sees* a column of random draws and summary statistics, and numbers that change at every keystroke. *The program sees* RAND, RANDARRAY or RANDBETWEEN feeding many rows, or a data table driven by an unused cell (likely). *Correct by* naming the trial count and the outputs. *Classic:* a "volatile" note in Details. *Inspector:* how many cells recalculate on every change, and how long that takes. *Notebook:* a frame of trials and a histogram of the output. *Map:* a box marked `◊ volatile`. *App:* a "Draw again" control, which is F9.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-12 (Control panel): *A person sees* sliders, boxes and lists gathered on one sheet. *The program sees* form controls and their linked cells (certain); that the sheet is a panel is a guess. *Correct by* grouping or ungrouping the controls. *Inspector:* each control, its linked cell and what that reaches. *Notebook:* the controls, in line, live. *Map:* controls drawn on their boxes. *App:* the first draft of the page.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-13 (PivotTable): *A person sees* the banded layout and field buttons. *The program sees* the pivot and its cache (certain). *Correct by* nothing. *Classic:* freshness in Details. *Inspector:* source, last refresh, whether the source has changed. *Notebook:* a frame with its freshness line. *Map:* a box, "snapshot of Orders". *App:* a read-only table with Refresh.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-14 (Live data): *A person sees* numbers that move by themselves. *The program sees* RTD formulas, linked data types, web functions, NOW and TODAY (certain). *Correct by* nothing. *Classic:* `◊` in the overlay; the Strip's count of live topics. *Inspector:* the Live instrument: each source, its rate, its last value and time, and a strip of events. *Notebook:* values with their time of arrival. *Map:* source boxes in signal orange at the edge. *App:* a "live" mark and the time of the last update on any tile fed from outside.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.
evidence: D-14; none in the cast; Watershed's clock and price feed

statement: Pattern D-15 (Macro-driven model): *A person sees* buttons, and values that appear after pressing them. *The program sees* modules, the controls and events that call them (certain), and the ranges named in the code (likely). *Correct by* nothing; the user chooses whether to allow macros. *Classic:* buttons that explain when blocked. *Inspector:* procedures, callers, and the calls each makes. *Notebook:* a note where a macro writes into a block. *Map:* a "written by a macro" mark on those boxes. *App:* a button, behind the same trust card.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-16 (Report or dashboard): *A person sees* formatting, charts, few inputs and a print area. *The program sees* a sheet that nothing reads, with charts and a print area (guess). *Correct by* "This is an output" on a sheet or a block. *Inspector:* everything the report rests on. *Notebook:* the closing section, or the opening one under "Conclusions first". *Map:* the right-hand end. *App:* the outputs.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-17 (Stocks, flows, feedback and delays): *A person* thinks of it that way, or drew it that way. *The program sees* a state cell that adds some terms and subtracts others each period or pass, and chains of last-pass reads (guess, resting on D-9 and D-10). *Correct by* marking a cell as a stock, a flow or a delay. *Inspector:* the Calc instrument and Watch. *Notebook:* a narrated model, state items first. *Map:* its native form. *App:* controls, a step key and a chart of the stock.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-18 (Repeated sheets and 3-D sums): *A person sees* a row of tabs named for months or branches that look alike. *The program sees* sheets whose formulas match cell for cell (certain), and 3-D references across them (certain). *Correct by* adding or removing a sheet from the set. *Classic:* a set badge on each tab. *Inspector:* cells where one sheet of the set differs from the others. *Notebook:* one section with a sheet picker. *Map:* a stack, "12 alike". *App:* a picker.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-19 (Checks and reconciliations): *A person sees* cells that say OK, or a difference that should be zero. *The program sees* a formula comparing two totals and returning a flag, or the difference of two sums (likely). *Correct by* "This is a check" on any cell, with the value that counts as a pass. *Classic:* the Strip, "7 of 8 checks pass". *Inspector:* the list, failures first, each with both sides traced. *Notebook:* a line at the end of its section. *Map:* a small mark on the frame. *App:* a warning line when any check fails.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.
evidence: D-19; typical of a Budget; none in the cast file

statement: Pattern D-20 (Overrides and plugs): *A person* remembers typing it, or does not. *The program sees* a constant, or a formula with an added constant, inside a run (certain that the run is broken; a guess whether it is meant). *Correct by* "Noted exception", with a reason. *Classic:* Excel's own indicator, and the seam's warning when one is about to be made. *Inspector:* all exceptions, noted and not. *Notebook, Map:* "11 alike, 1 differs". *App:* a mark on any output that rests on an exception that has not been noted.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-21 (Linked workbooks): *A person sees* file names in formulas, or Excel's prompt. *The program sees* external references and the values saved for them (certain). *Correct by* pointing a missing link at a file, which is Excel's Edit Links. *Classic:* `◊`. *Inspector:* the Links list: found or missing, last updated, cells fed. *Notebook:* the source named under the frame it feeds. *Map:* boxes at the edge. *App:* a "from another file, as saved" mark.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-22 (Switches and modes): *A person sees* a cell holding 1 or 2, TRUE or FALSE, or a word. *The program sees* IFS, SWITCH, CHOOSE or nested IF on one cell (likely). *Correct by* naming the cases. *Inspector:* the formulas each case turns on. *Notebook:* a control with the cases named. *Map:* a mode box listing the cases, the current one marked. *App:* a toggle or a list.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-23 (Goal Seek and Solver set-ups): *A person* remembers running it. *The program sees* Solver's saved settings (certain); for Goal Seek nothing is stored, so only a guess from a result that sits exactly on a round target. *Correct by* nothing for Solver. *Inspector:* target, changing cells and limits. *Notebook:* a note, "solved for X by changing Y". *Map:* a dashed link from the target back to the changing cells. *App:* nothing by default.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-24 (Form or document): *A person sees* an invoice or a statement: merged cells, borders, a logo. *The program sees* many merged cells, borders, a print area and few formulas (guess). *Correct by* "This is a form". *Classic:* as it is; this is Classic's ground. *Inspector:* the few cells that feed it. *Notebook, Map:* one item, "a printed form", with its inputs. *App:* its blank cells as fields, if the user asks.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-25 (Scratch and dead areas): *A person sees* workings off to the right that nobody mentions. *The program sees* cells that nothing reads and that are not a report (certain that they are unread; a guess that they are scratch). *Correct by* "Keep in view" or "This is an output". *Inspector:* the list, with sizes. *Notebook:* folded under "not used by anything". *Map:* a collapsed group. *App:* nothing.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-26 (Named formulas and LAMBDA libraries): *A person sees* names in the Name Manager that hold formulas. *The program sees* names bound to LAMBDA or to a formula (certain). *Correct by* nothing. *Inspector:* where each is used. *Notebook:* a definitions section. *Map:* definition boxes, drawn once and referred to by name. *App:* nothing. *Formula Explorer:* they appear in the function list and can be called and stepped into.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.

statement: Pattern D-27 (Two-way table): *A person sees* a grid with headings on two sides and one formula everywhere. *The program sees* a rectangle of formulas with one row-fixed and one column-fixed reference (likely). *Correct by* naming the two axes. *Inspector:* one run in two directions; exceptions. *Notebook:* one formula item with both axes named, and a frame. *Map:* one box with two inputs. *App:* a shaded table.
why: Defines human recognition, program evidence/grade, correction gesture, and per-view rendering.
evidence: D-27; typical of price lists and allocations
